describes: Surface cues for lowering free text into the deontic language, as DATA — sufficient on its own for a generic consumer (the ingest plane) to extract deterministically without importing any deontic code. deontic's own reference producer, deontic.prose (used by the plane descriptor), does NOT read this file at runtime: Phase 1 replaced the regex walk with a stdlib recursive-descent parser (deontic.prose_grammar) driven by the JSON gazetteers under artifacts/gazetteer/*.json — that parser's single source of cues. This file stays the single, self-sufficient surface for a consumer that does not want to import deontic code at all, and tools/check_extraction.py's gazetteer-sync gate holds every gazetteer-published cue (modal phrases, negation adverbs, negating interposed phrases, condition leads/tails, exception leads) equal to (covered by) this file's regex, so the two published surfaces cannot drift apart. The regex sources here are also held equal to the language modules (deontic.incidents) by tools/check_extraction.py; the modal cues (surface phrase -> modal class) are the one piece the package deliberately does not carry in code, published here for consumers. The deadline_cues, cross_reference_cues, and sanction_cues are additive: they populate the optional carry fields (deadline / cross_references / sanction) added to statement.schema.json; like the modal cues they are published as data only, carried nowhere in code (opaque text the reasoning layer types, resolves, and applies). Each named group holds the extracted value; the FULL match is the cue's published surface (a consumer that records or removes the surface anchors on the full match, so the clause-level deadline entries deliberately cover the whole deadline clause — connective, feasibility qualifier, cue, value, reference-point tail — while the named group still holds only the value). The validity_cues lower CONSTITUTIVE validity norms (a term 'is void' / 'ist unwirksam' directs no conduct; it denies legal effect): each cue carries an effect (void / preserved / substitution), and validity_rules maps an effect to the Hohfeldian incident borne by the norm's addressee — void is the drafter's disability to give the term legal effect (the counterparty's immunity follows via the published correlatives); preserved and substitution abstain ('') as consequence shapes with no single addressee incident. Validity is NOT a fourth modal operator: the operator set stays O/P/F, and validity lives in the constitutive/incident layer the language already publishes. slot_cues.condition_tail lifts a trailing condition clause ('before it is sent') into the condition slot, mirroring the gazetteer-driven parser's own condition_tail production (artifacts/gazetteer/condition.json's tail_leads); where the trailing phrase is not a clause ('after use') deontic.prose abstains rather than choose between condition and adverbial. Round 4 (deontic-is-ought correction): this file publishes no operator->5D binding; the earlier operator_axis key is removed. Operators (O/P/F) are ought; the 5D describes what is; a norm's content enters 5D through the factual plane, not through the operator. deontic.contract.dimension_affinity and deontic.plane.binding are total functions that answer with no dimension for any operator. Round 5 defect (a), generalised: a negation adverb after a modal ("not", "never", "at no time"), with or without interposed commas or an interposed phrase (e.g. "shall never, under any circumstances,"), lowers the modal to F (prohibition), with the negation adverb and any interposed phrase consumed by the matched cue so neither reaches `action` nor is duplicated onto `negated` — the same convention "must not"/"shall not" already carry. slot_cues.condition_lead covers 'if'/'where'/'when'/'provided that'/'subject to'/'in the event of', each sentence-initial, stripped from the published condition; condition_lead stays sentence-initial-only by design (a lead phrase appearing after the modal is not lifted into condition — see deontic.prose_grammar.analyze's documented grammar, condition as a sibling constituent of modal_frame, never nested inside it). 'in the case of' is NOT a condition lead: it is a genuine condition on some real text but a bare scope/topic marker with no conditional force on other real text, and the surface alone cannot tell the two apart — an ambiguous lead is not consumed (see artifacts/gazetteer/condition.json's describes for the worked examples). slot_cues.condition_lead_with_phrase covers 'at the request of'/'upon the request of'/'in such a case': its named group captures the lead's own words AS PART OF the condition, because stripping the lead would either lose the request itself ('at the request of the data subject' is a request, not only a party) or, for the anaphoric 'in such a case', publish an EMPTY condition indistinguishable from an unconditional duty (see deontic.prose_grammar's keep_lead mechanism, same gazetteer entries, artifacts/gazetteer/condition.json). slot_cues.exception_lead does NOT include 'by way of derogation from' or 'abweichend von': 'by way of derogation from X, R' means R OVERRIDES X — R is the exception to X, not the other way round — so modelling it as this rule's OWN exception would invert the relation; it is not modelled as anything else either (see artifacts/gazetteer/exception.json's describes). The pre-existing bare 'abweichend' alternative here is UNCHANGED and stays a known, out-of-scope issue (it captures an entire German main rule as if it were an exception on the regex surface). incident_cues.power_verb is word-anchored to explicit finite-verb forms wherever a bare stem+\w* wildcard also spelled an unrelated common noun/adjective: elect\w* matched "electronic"/"election"/"elector"/"electoral"; withdraw\w* matched "withdrawal"; waive\w* matched "waiver"; approv\w* matched "approval"; authoris\w*/authoriz\w* matched "authorisation"/"authorization"; assign\w* matched "assignment"/"assignable"; renew\w* matched "renewal"; instruct\w* matched "instruction(s)"/"instructor". Each of those eight is now anchored to its explicit finite-verb inflections (irregular ones spelled out, e.g. withdraw/withdraws/withdrawing/withdrew/withdrawn) instead of stem+\w*; "authorised"/"authorized" is additionally excluded immediately before "representative(s)" (a defined role, not an exercised power). terminat\w*/rescind\w*/revoke\w*/consent\w*/suspend\w* were checked and found with no such collision (left unchanged); exercis\w* is left unchanged on purpose ("exercise" is the identical spelling for the noun and the verb in English — no word-anchoring can separate them); the German stems are also left unchanged (German nominalises most of them with the same stem+"-ung" pattern, and two are zero-derivation like "exercise" — see deontic.incidents._POWER_VERBS's own comment for the full account). "require" is deliberately NOT a power_verb regex alternative: a permission to require something of another party is a Hohfeldian power, but only the exact active forms "require"/"requires"/"requiring" count — never any form of "required", since a passive or reduced-relative "required" ("as required under Article 6", "information required to assess compliance") has no reliable surface cue separating it from an active one — and the check runs over the action span ONLY, never the whole raw sentence. This is published as structured DATA below, require_power_cue, that a generic consumer can apply by plain word membership without importing any deontic code or compiling a regex, held equal to deontic.incidents._has_active_require's own constants by tools/check_extraction.py, and wired into incident_rules (when_matches: "require_power_cue") so the published rules surface reproduces classify_incident's "require" reading, not only its power_verb reading. classify_incident's modal=="obligation" branch returns "duty" before ever consulting power_verb or require_power_cue, so "require" inside an obligation's own action text is never misread as a power/disability. The permission modal_cues alternation did not originally carry the "shall be" forms real EU legislation uses alongside the bare "is"/"are" forms (DSA Art. 60(4) "shall be entitled to", GDPR Art. 12(8) "shall be empowered to"), so the bare obligation "shall" won instead of the permission the longer phrase lexicalises. "shall be entitled to"/"are entitled to"/"shall be empowered to"/"shall be authorised to"/"shall be authorized to"/"shall have the power to" are now published modal_cues[permission] alternatives, mirroring the gazetteer's modal_lexemes.json entries (Gate F). Every one of these six also contains the literal word "shall" (except "are entitled to", which contains no obligation word at all), so modal_cues[obligation]'s own \bshall\b ALSO matches their full text: this is not an oversight. The tie-break a plain, code-free consumer must apply when more than one modal_cues pattern matches the same span is 'the pattern naming the LONGER literal phrase wins' — the same longest-match-first rule modal_lexemes.json's own gazetteer-driven parser already applies at a single token position (see that file's own describes field); tools/check_extraction.py's Gate H proves this tie-break actually resolves every such overlap in this file (the permission phrase is always strictly longer, in words, than the bare obligation lexeme it overlaps with) rather than merely asserting it. Gate H does not change array order and does not require one: a consumer that checks `permission` and finds a match is never contradicted by this file reordering `modal_cues` later, because the tie-break is stated as a property OF THE MATCHED TEXT (longer literal phrase), not of this array's position. incident_cues.power_verb now also carries "empower"/"empowers"/"empowered"/"empowering" (explicit finite-verb forms, word-anchored against the noun "empowerment" the same way authoris/authoriz already are) and the phrase alternative "(?:have|has) the power to", so "shall be empowered to"/"shall have the power to" read as a Hohfeldian power regardless of which verb follows (adopt, order, impose, require, ...), not only a bare permission; "authorised to"/"authorized to" already reached power through the pre-existing authoris/authoriz alternatives, and "entitled to" carries no power_verb cue of its own and stays a privilege by default. A plain modal_cues[permission] match on one of those same six phrases is not, by itself, sufficient to accept a permission reading: complement_verb_cue (below) is an ADDITIVE condition over the word immediately following the match — see its own describes field for why (a noun/adjective/gerund/possessive complement after 'entitled to'/'empowered to'/'have the power to' is a claim-object or not an infinitive at all, never a liberty/power to act, and is not caught by checking the matched cue's text alone).

modal_cues.pattern: \b(?:shall not|must not|may not|(?:shall|must|may)(?:\s*,\s*|\s+)(?:never|at\s+no\s+time)\s*,?\s*(?:[^,.;]+?,\s*)?|is not permitted to|is prohibited from|darf\s+\w+\s+nicht|darf nicht)\b
\b(?:shall|must|is obliged to|is required to|has to|muss|m(?:ü|u)ssen|hat zu)\b

\b(?:may|is permitted to|is free to|is entitled to|are entitled to|shall be entitled to|shall be empowered to|shall be authorised to|shall be authorized to|shall have the power to|is authorised to|darf|kann)\b

slot_cues.condition_lead_with_phrase: ^\s*(?P<cond>(?:at the request of|upon the request of|in such a case)\b.*?),
slot_cues.exception_lead: \b(?:unless|except|save where|save as|without prejudice to|es sei denn|abweichend)\b\s*(?P<exc>.*)$

complement_verb_cue.describes: The six permission modal_cues alternatives listed in applies_to_modal_cues only read as a permission when the word immediately after the matched cue is, case-insensitively, one of the base-form verbs below, AND the word right after THAT (if any) is not one of noun_markers or, for a verb listed in verb_specific_noun_markers, one of its own extra markers — mirrors deontic.prose_grammar's requires_verb_complement gate (artifacts/gazetteer/modal_lexemes.json's own per-entry flags) and artifacts/gazetteer/complement_verbs.json (that file's own describes field records the corpus derivation of this exact list), held equal to both by tools/check_extraction.py. A plain, code-free consumer that only reads modal_cues would otherwise misread a noun/adjective/gerund/possessive complement as the SAME permission a genuine infinitival action is ('are entitled to COMPENSATION', 'shall be entitled to FAIR compensation', 'shall be entitled to PAID annual leave', 'shall be entitled to RECEIVING compensation', 'shall have the power to ITS own investigative powers' all name a claim-object or are not an infinitive at all, never a liberty/power to act) — checking the matched cue's own text ALONE is not enough; this condition is additive, applied AFTER a modal_cues[permission] match on one of the six listed phrases. The second check catches a homograph the first word alone cannot: 'transfer'/'charge'/'record'/'claim'/'share'/'address'/'act'/'request'/'use'/'control'/'process'/'order' are all listed verbs that are ALSO common nouns, and 'of'/'for' right after one of them ('entitled to TRANSFER OF the data', 'entitled to ADDRESS FOR service') is exactly the noun reading's own signature, never the verb one ('order THE controller to comply' keeps working: its second word is 'the', not a marker); 'access' gets the single extra marker 'to' of its own, because 'access' the VERB is monotransitive ('access THE FILE') while 'access' the NOUN regularly takes 'to' ('a right of access TO the file'). A word not in the verb list, or a verb whose own complement fails the marker check, does not mean the sentence is OBLIGATION or PROHIBITION instead: for FIVE of the six phrases (every one except 'shall have the power to') it means this one permission reading does not apply, and a careful consumer falls back to treating the sentence as covered only by whichever OTHER modal_cues pattern also matches the same text (typically the bare obligation lexeme 'shall', which then itself abstains on the consumer's own terms — the remaining text opens on 'be', already a recognised state/passive lead with no resolvable action). 'shall have the power to' (named in no_fallback_modal_cue below) is the one exception: unlike the other five, its own 'shall'-alone fallback does NOT abstain on its own terms (the remaining text opens on 'have', not 'be'), so a careful consumer must treat a failed check on THIS phrase as the sentence abstaining outright — never falling back to read it as an obligation.

require_power_cue.describes: A permission/right to require something of another party is a Hohfeldian power (classify_incident -> 'power'), and the removal of that power under a prohibition is a disability — but only the exact active forms below, applied to the ACTION span only, never the whole raw sentence. Mirrors deontic.incidents._has_active_require and skills/deontic/deontic_engine._has_active_require exactly, and is wired into incident_rules below (when_matches: 'require_power_cue') so the published rules surface reproduces the same reading.

cross_reference_cues.instrument: \b(?:in accordance with|pursuant to|as (?:set out|referred to|provided|specified) in|under|subject to|gem(?:ä|a)(?:ß|ss)|nach|im Sinne (?:des|der))\s+(?P<ref>(?:Article|Art\.?|Section|Sec\.?|§|Regulation|Directive|Annex|Artikel|Absatz|Abs\.?|Anhang)\s*[\w.()/\-]+)

sanction_cues.lead: \b(?:on pain of|under penalty of|subject to (?:a\s+)?(?:penalty|fine|sanction)|shall be (?:liable|punishable)|punishable by|liable to (?:a\s+)?(?:fine|penalty)|unter Androhung|bei (?:Androhung|Strafe|Vermeidung))\b(?P<sanction>[^.]*)
